truth.authoringRationale: A STOP selector is not an isolation, and an arm through the manway of a blanketed vessel is a stated present exposure. evidence.quotedText: its explosion vent panel painted over

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: The explosion vent panel, which is the deflagration relief device for the dust collector, is painted over, which can prevent it from functioning (rupturing/venting) if a deflagration occurs inside the collector.
expertHazardCandidates.reasoning: A painted-over explosion vent panel is a defeated or degraded explosion relief device on a vessel handling combustible metal dust while grinding is actively in progress, so a deflagration event occurring now would not be safely vented, increasing the severity of the existing combustible dust hazard into an uncontrolled explosion risk.

evidence.quotedText: its ductwork visibly loaded with fine metal dust

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: Ductwork is described as visibly loaded with fine metal dust while grinding is in progress.

source.observation: A technician was cleaning the spray booth extract plenum with an aerosolised solvent while kneeling inside the booth. The booth extract fan was switched off for the cleaning and the booth doors were closed. Two other workers were spraying primer in the adjacent bay, which shares a return-air path with the booth. The observation does not record what respiratory protection, if any, the technician inside the booth was wearing.

decisionCriticalGaps.description: what respiratory protection the technician inside the booth was wearing while the extract fan was off

truth.authoringRationale: Solvent aerosol inside a closed booth with the extract off is a stated present inhalation exposure. Respiratory protection bears on THAT candidate and on no other: it does not touch the shared-return-air fire concern and it does not touch the walking surface. The two answers give two different current actions -- an appropriate supplied-air or cartridge respirator in use means the exposure is controlled and the finding is the fan interlock; nothing worn means immediate withdrawal from the booth. That is the REQUIRED test satisfied by a question whose FORM is about PPE, which is exactly the collision v8 could not decide.

decisionCriticalGaps.description: whether the muting arrangement on these presses has been through the site authorisation process, which the observation leaves open for both machines identically

truth.authoringRationale: AMBIGUOUS REFERENT BY CONSTRUCTION. Two presses in the same family, in the same state, with the same defect. Any authorisation question applies to both identically, so a model that raises two guarding candidates has no unique referent to name.

evidence.quotedText: were running with their light curtains muted

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: Both presses are currently operating with their point-of-operation light curtain guarding deliberately muted while operators load blanks by hand.
expertHazardCandidates.reasoning: Muting a light curtain disables the presence-sensing guard that would otherwise stop the press stroke when a hand enters the danger zone. Because operators are loading blanks by hand at both presses while the curtains are muted, the guarding function is currently defeated during a task that puts hands in the point of operation, creating an active struck-by/crush exposure.

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: The physical key that activates the mute override is left in place in the panel rather than controlled/removed.
expertHazardCandidates.reasoning: Leaving the override key in the panel means any operator or other person can engage or re-engage the mute function without authorization or accountability, removing the administrative control that is meant to limit who can defeat the guard and when.

evidence.quotedText: The observation does not record whether either machine has been through the site muting-authorisation process.

source.observation: The roof access hatch on the plant room was propped open with a length of conduit and the fixed ladder below it runs twenty feet to the floor. There is no cover, no guardrail and no gate at the hatch opening. The observation does not establish whether anyone is scheduled to work on the roof while the hatch is propped.

decisionCriticalGaps.description: whether anyone is scheduled to work on the roof, and therefore to pass the propped-open hatch, during the period it is propped

truth.authoringRationale: Two branches with different current actions: work scheduled means close or guard the opening and control access now; no access until the hatch is restored means the correction can be scheduled. A general positive clarification control, retained because a linkage probe that produced no questions at all would measure nothing.

evidence.quotedText: There is no cover, no guardrail and no gate at the hatch opening.

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: The hatch opening itself is left unguarded on an active walking-working surface (roof/plant room), independent of whether a fall exposure at the ladder is confirmed.
expertHazardCandidates.reasoning: An unguarded floor/roof opening with no cover, guardrail, or gate is itself a hazardous walking-working surface condition — anyone moving across the plant room floor or roof near the propped hatch could step into the opening, regardless of whether scheduled roof work is occurring.

evidence.quotedText: propped open with a length of conduit

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: An improvised prop (length of conduit) is being used to hold the hatch open instead of a designed hold-open device.
expertHazardCandidates.reasoning: Using a loose length of conduit as a prop is an unsecured object at height over an opening with a 20-foot drop below; if it slips or is dislodged, the hatch could fall shut or the conduit itself could fall through the opening, creating a struck-by exposure at the base of the ladder.

decisionCriticalClarifications.question: Is any employee currently scheduled or expected to access the roof through this hatch while it remains propped open and unguarded?
decisionCriticalClarifications.whyItMatters: If a worker is scheduled to use the hatch now, the fall exposure is confirmed and immediate fall protection (guardrail, cover, or personal fall arrest) must be implemented before any access; if no one is scheduled to access it, the priority is to secure or cover the opening to prevent incidental exposure until it is needed, which is a different and less urgent control action.
decisionCriticalClarifications.evidenceGap: The observation explicitly states it does not establish whether anyone is scheduled to work on the roof while the hatch is propped open.

expertExplanation.summary: The deterministic engine correctly flags fall protection as unresolved because employee access to the roof hatch is not established, but the unguarded hatch opening itself (no cover, guardrail, or gate) is a current walking-working-surface hazard independent of scheduled roof work, and the conduit used to prop it open is an additional, lower-confidence struck-by/dislodgement concern given the 20-foot drop below. The single missing fact that would resolve the primary decision is whether anyone is currently scheduled to access the roof through this hatch, since that determines whether immediate personal fall protection is required versus simply securing the opening.

source.observation: A contractor was hot-tapping a live process line under a permit. The permit lists a fire watch but the observation records no one standing watch at the work location, and combustible lagging is within a metre of the tap point. What the line carries is not recorded on the permit copy at the job.

governedStandards.title: Respiratory protection program
governedStandards.approvedText: In any workplace where respirators are necessary to protect the health of the employee, the employer shall establish and implement a written respiratory protection program with worksite-specific procedures, as set out at 29 CFR 1910.134(c)(1).

decisionCriticalGaps.description: what the live line being hot-tapped actually carries

truth.authoringRationale: The contents decide the magnitude and therefore the current action: an inert or aqueous service means the finding is the missing fire watch and the lagging; a flammable or toxic service means stopping the hot work now. The second general positive clarification control, in an unrelated family from CL-T1.

evidence.quotedText: the observation records no one standing watch at the work location

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: The permit requires a fire watch but none is present at the work location during active hot-tapping of a live process line.
expertHazardCandidates.reasoning: Hot work is in progress on a live process line, the permit mandates a fire watch as a control, and that control is absent at the point of work right now. This is a stated current gap, not a historical or hypothetical condition.

evidence.quotedText: combustible lagging is within a metre of the tap point

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: Combustible material is currently located close to the point of hot work.
expertHazardCandidates.reasoning: Hot-tapping produces sparks, heat, or slag; combustible lagging within a metre of the tap point is a current ignition exposure that exists independent of the fire watch gap.

evidence.quotedText: What the line carries is not recorded on the permit copy at the job

expertHazardCandidates.evidenceBasis: The contents of the live process line being hot-tapped are not documented on the permit at the job site.
expertHazardCandidates.reasoning: Hot-tapping a live line whose contents are unknown at the work location creates a possible chemical release or flammable-contents exposure if the line carries a hazardous substance; this cannot be confirmed from the observation alone.

decisionCriticalClarifications.question: What does the process line being hot-tapped actually carry?
decisionCriticalClarifications.whyItMatters: If the line carries a flammable or hazardous substance, the hot-tap creates a fire/explosion or chemical release exposure requiring immediate work stoppage and specialized controls; if it carries an inert or non-hazardous substance, the hot-tap can proceed under standard hot work controls. The permit copy at the job does not state which, and the correct response differs materially between the two.
decisionCriticalClarifications.evidenceGap: The permit copy at the work location does not record the contents of the line being tapped.

crossHazardInsights.reasoning: Hot-tapping generates sparks/heat capable of igniting combustible lagging located within a metre of the tap point; the absence of a fire watch means an ignition of that lagging would go undetected and unresponded to until it escalates, whereas either condition alone (lagging with a watch present, or a watch absent but no combustibles nearby) would not produce the same fire escalation risk.

expertExplanation.summary: The observation describes active hot-tapping of a live process line with two current control gaps: the permit-required fire watch is absent from the work location, and combustible lagging sits within a metre of the tap point — together these mean a spark-ignited fire could go undetected. A further gap is that the permit copy at the job does not record what the line carries, which leaves open whether the hot-tap is exposing workers to a flammable or hazardous substance release, a fact that changes whether the work can safely continue as-is. No governed record supplied addresses hot work, fire watch, or process line content controls, so no regulatory obligation is asserted here beyond what the observation itself shows.
